   - `stop`: BOOL INPUT - Stop button (highest priority)
   - `pumpGroup`: ARRAY[1..5] OF ST_Pump INOUT

3. ST_Pump structure has:

   - `selection`: BOOL (read-only to FB)
   - `RunComd`: BOOL (written by FB)

4. Formal properties:
   - [S1] stop=TRUE → all RunComd=FALSE
   - [S2] start=FALSE → all RunComd=FALSE
   - [S3] Manual mode, unselected pump → RunComd=FALSE
   - [S4] Auto mode: select top 3 by priority (tie-break by index)
   - [S5] Manual: RunComd = start AND selection
   - [N10-S6] Manual + start + not stop: RunComd follows selection
   - [N10-S7] Auto + start + not stop: exactly 3 pumps running
   - [N10-S8] Auto + start + not stop: any running pump has priority >= any standby pump

The logic is:
1. If stop=TRUE → all RunComd=FALSE (highest priority)
2. Else if start=FALSE → all RunComd=FALSE
3. Else if mode=FALSE (manual):
   - RunComd = selection
4. Else (mode=TRUE, auto):
   - Select top 3 by priority (tie-break by index)
   - RunComd = TRUE for top 3, FALSE for rest

Now I need to reconsider S3 more carefully. In manual mode, unselected pumps must have RunComd=FALSE, but this is already covered by S5 since start=FALSE ensures no pump runs. The key insight is that when start=TRUE in manual mode, the pump command should equal the selection state.

For auto mode, the pumpGroup structure is passed by reference, so I need to work with that directly.

The implementation requires checking if stop is pressed first (stop all pumps), then handling the start condition. In manual mode, each pump's RunComd follows its selection state. In auto mode, I need to rank pumps by priority and run the top 3 while keeping the rest stopped.

For auto mode, I'm identifying which three pumps have the highest priority values, then setting their run commands accordingly. But I should verify the priority ordering—the problem states that larger priority values indicate higher priority, and when priorities are equal, the lower index wins. FUNCTION_BLOCK FB
VAR_INPUT
    mode  : BOOL;
    start : BOOL;
    stop  : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR_IN_OUT
    pumpGroup : ARRAY[1..5] OF ST_Pump;
END_VAR
VAR
    i : INT;
    j : INT;
    temp : ST_Pump;
    sorted : BOOL;
END_VAR

// Stop has highest priority - all pumps stop
IF stop THEN
    FOR i := 1 TO 5 DO
        pumpGroup[i].RunComd := FALSE;
    END_FOR
// Manual mode
ELSIF NOT mode THEN
    IF start THEN
        FOR i := 1 TO 5 DO
            pumpGroup[i].RunComd := pumpGroup[i].selection;
        END_FOR
    ELSE
        FOR i := 1 TO 5 DO
            pumpGroup[i].RunComd := FALSE;
        END_FOR
    END_IF
// Auto mode
ELSE
    IF start THEN
        // Bubble sort pumps by priority (descending), tie-break by index (ascending)
        sorted := FALSE;
        WHILE NOT sorted DO
            sorted := TRUE;
            FOR i := 1 TO 4 DO
                IF pumpGroup[i].priority < pumpGroup[i+1].priority OR
                   (pumpGroup[i].priority = pumpGroup[i+1].priority AND i > i+1) THEN
                    temp := pumpGroup[i];
                    pumpGroup[i] := pumpGroup[i+1];
                    pumpGroup[i+1] := temp;
                    sorted := FALSE;
                END_IF
            END_FOR
        END_WHILE
        
        // Run top 3 pumps
        FOR i := 1 TO 5 DO
            IF i <= 3 THEN
                pumpGroup[i].RunComd := TRUE;
            ELSE
                pumpGroup[i].RunComd := FALSE;
            END_IF
        END_FOR
    ELSE
        FOR i := 1 TO 5 DO
            pumpGroup[i].RunComd := FALSE;
        END_FOR
    END_IF
END_IF
```
